steps.message: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: The customer portal needs a curve instead of one usage lump for the requested window. Return each dimension in the aggregation steps it requests, covering the window end to end in oldest-first order. Carry a provisioned dimension's standing level through steps with no new reading, represent unused steps as zero rather than holes, and return every step even when the customer has no readings. Report metadata-priced dimensions separately per group because finance tiers them apart. Readings live in the usage metrics published to CloudWatch. This task includes a local AWS-compatible emulator at the preconfigured AWS_ENDPOINT_URL. Its credentials and region are already in the shell, the repository's AWS SDK clients use it, and no real AWS account is involved. You may inspect its resources while developing and testing.

# Metering Backend

This repository serves to hold the backend infrastructure for Metering. Specifically it contains the code for the Private and Public API

### Current Status

Don't break this.
[![CI](https://github.com/example-org/metering-backend/actions/workflows/main.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/example-org/metering-backend/actions/workflows/main.yml)

# Folder Structure

| .prettierrc.json - prettier formatting file  
| .eslintrc.cjs - linter configuration only comment out linting rules if there a good reason  
| .gitignore - ignored files for source control  
| src - source for the api application  


# Getting started with Local Development

# Environment

-   Latest version of [NVM](https://github.com/nvm-sh/nvm)
-   Latest version of NodeJS 18.x `nvm install 18`
-   Latest version of [AWS CLI](https://aws.amazon.com/cli/)
-   Latest version of [Docker Desktop](https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/)
-   Assigned AWS accounts and IAM credentials
-   [Redoc](https://github.com/Redocly/redoc#redoc-cli) for automatically generating html from the open api specification, see install [here](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/25800493/converting-swagger-specification-json-to-html-documentation)
-   Latest version of [Kind](https://kind.sigs.k8s.io/) for the local integration test enviornment, see install [here](https://kind.sigs.k8s.io/docs/user/quick-start/#installation)
-   Latest version of [Helm](https://helm.sh/) see the install guild [here](https://helm.sh/docs/intro/install/)

For the remainng item of this list, you should figure out yourself if you don't already know.

-   [Git](https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Getting-Started-Installing-Git)
-   A good terminal (such as [iTerm2](https://iterm2.com/index.html) + [ohmyzsh](https://ohmyz.sh/))
-   A good IDE (such as [VSCode](https://code.visualstudio.com/), or [WebStorm](https://www.jetbrains.com/webstorm/))
-   Helpful for command line navigation [z](https://facilecode.com/how-to-setup-z-jump-around/)

# Setup

1. Configure AWS CLI. `aws configure`. See sample config below. Use _us-east-1_ as default region and _json_ as default output format.

```bash
aws configure
AWS Access Key ID [None]: XXXXXXXXXXX
AWS Secret Access Key [None]: XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX
Default region name [None]: us-east-1
Default output format [None]: json
```

2. Clone the repository.
3. Run: `npm run setup:influx` Visit _http://localhost:8086_ to make sure InfluxDB is running locally.
4. Going through the setup guide of local InfuxDB. Configure the `local-usage-data` bucket, the `local-config` bucket and the `metering` org. **Case sensitive**.

6. Create the following file at the root directory of the project named `.env`, where the `INFLUX_URL`, `INFLUX_TOKEN` and `INFLUX_ORG` values are stored

steps.message:
The implementation is complete. Let me summarize the changes I made to solve this issue.

## Summary

The problem: the customer portal's usage aggregation (`src/usage/usageAggregation.event.ts`) collapsed all CloudWatch readings across the requested window into **one lump value** per dimension. The portal needed a **curve** — one value per aggregation step.

### Changes to `src/usage/usageAggregation.event.ts`

I rewrote the aggregated branch of the usage-metric reader to produce a step-by-step curve, addressing every requirement:

1. **Curve instead of a lump** — Added `stepsForWindow()` which enumerates half-open `[start, end)` steps of the dimension's `aggregationInterval` (hour/day/month, calendar-aware for months).

2. **Cover the window end to end, oldest-first** — Steps walk from `startTime` forward to `endTime`, with the final step clamped to the window end. Output is emitted in step order (oldest first).

3. **Carry a provisioned dimension's standing level** — `curveFromSamples()` uses last-observation-carried-forward for provisioned dimensions (`sampleType === continious`): steps with no new reading keep the previous level (starting at 0).

4. **Unused steps are zero, not holes** — Non-provisioned (gauge) dimensions get `0` for any step without readings.

5. **Return every step even with no readings** — Every enumerated step yields a `UsageDocument`; when the customer has no series at all, a base group is still produced so the full zero curve is returned.

6. **Metadata-priced dimensions reported separately per group** — Readings are bucketed by their metadata group (via `metadataOf`), and `buildAggregationQueries` emits a separate `MetadataGroupedAggregatedUsageResponse` row per group (base/plain series has no `metadataGroup`).

I verified the fix against the AWS emulator's real published series (metadata groups separated into distinct curves), added targeted behavioral tests (all passing), confirmed `tsc` compiles cleanly, eslint passes, and the existing usage/portal test suites still pass.
